newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Mercury bids for more Power NZ shares.
newsitem.headline: Mercury bids for more Power NZ shares.

text.p: Auckland's Mercury Energy said on Monday it would make oral offers to WEL Energy and local authority shareholders in Power New Zealand Ltd to buy their PNZ shares at prices ranging from NZ$7.25 to $10/share.
Mercury said the offers will be for a maximum of 12.1 million shares or eight percent of PNZ, which would raise its stake in the company to 40.6 percent.
The offers will be made to the WEL Energy Group and to the district councils of Thames-Coromandel, Matamata-Piako, South Waikato, Hauraki, Waipa, the Western Bay of Plenty and Waikato.
The eight local authorities own 7.1 percent of Power New Zealand.
Offers will be made on or before September 20, and may be withdrawn at any time.
Mercury is waging a long-running battle for Power NZ shares with Utilicorp New Zealand, which is 79 percent owned by Utilicorp United Inc
